About the Project

Queen Mary’s organ-on-a-chip CDT trains doctoral researchers in bioengineering and predictive in vitro models. The 2027 recruitment round is expected to open in late November 2026.

Research Areas

  • Organ-on-a-chip technologies
  • bioengineering and predictive in vitro models

Funding and duration

ComponentDetails
FundingFees and stipend; International fully funded places are limited under programme terms.
MaintenanceGBP 23,805/year including London allowance (2026/27 reference)
Duration4 years

Eligibility and Requirements

Relevant preparation for bioengineering and predictive in vitro models; check current academic and fee-status conditions. English evidence, approved equivalents and waivers depend on the programme; IELTS is not a universal requirement for every applicant.

Application dates

ComponentDetails
Recruitment2027 opening expected late November 2026
Deadline2027 deadline pending; applications expected late November 2026

How to Apply

Follow the CDT step-by-step application guide when the 2027 round opens. Its presently linked portal reports that the selected period is unavailable.

Research focuses on next-generation organ-on-a-chip technologies. The older programme portal is not a live 2027 application form.

About Queen Mary University of London

Queen Mary University of London offers doctoral research across its schools and institutes. Its Centre for Predictive in vitro Models hosts doctoral training in organ-on-a-chip technologies and related bioengineering.
